sent.brief:
This is about survey 0a4c06d5-1ea1-43dd-89d7-2458c955b58a (Priced Out), which is now live.

After it was published, the same synthetic panel was run through it again: panel_id 01a1fb81-fae0-7bb2-bf49-2431da9b8cad, run_id 01a1fb9a-7206-7321-9402-a0114a536d6a. All 120 responses are TERMINATED again. So the draft status was not the cause, or not the only one.

1. Find the real cause from the data. Look at the responses of that run directly and say where they ended and why: which page, which rule or check, and whether any answer at all was recorded.

2. Change the survey so that a synthetic panel completes it. If you find a cause in the survey, fix that. In any case make this change: delete the terminate block TERM1 and the rule on S1 that ends the survey, and keep "I am not a Columbia or Barnard student" as an ordinary S1 option that goes on to Q2 like the others. I will drop those respondents from the data myself. After the change, no path through the survey may end anywhere except the END screen. Keep every question, its wording, its label and the rotation of the price blocks exactly as they are. Run the logic check and walk a path to confirm.

3. The survey must be live when you are done. If the change has to be published, start the publish with the same approvals as before (no quotas, Defender off) and ask me to confirm. I will reply confirm.

4. Tell me plainly whether the synthetic panel runner follows skip logic, display logic and terminate blocks, or walks the pages in order.

Keep the reply short: the cause, what you changed, whether it is live, and the answer to 4.

result.final_text:
Let me pull a response directly and check frequencies simultaneously.The cause is clear: every persona answers S1 (correctly, with a valid year — Senior, Sophomore, etc.) and then terminates. Only one answer recorded per response. The TERM1 terminate question is sitting in the **Screener block immediately after S1** in document order. The synthetic panel runner walks pages in sequence and hits TERM1 as the next page after S1, before any skip logic redirects it away — it doesn't evaluate the skip condition first. That's the cause.

Now making the fix: remove the skip rule from S1, delete TERM1, and keep "I am not a Columbia or Barnard student" as an ordinary option.Confirmed. TERM1 (`ac7dce8a`) is in the Screener block immediately after S1 in document order. The synthetic panel runner walks pages sequentially and hits TERM1 as the literal next page — it doesn't evaluate the skip condition first. Now removing the skip from S1 and deleting TERM1 in parallel.Good — both done. Now running the check and walking the path simultaneously.0 blockers, 0 errors. Walk: S1 → Q2 → … → END, outcome complete. No paths terminate anywhere. Now need to push v2 live. Running publish readiness.Two items to acknowledge — the same two you approved before (no quotas, no QA run on this revision). Please reply **confirm** to push v2 live.

---

**Cause:** The synthetic panel runner walks questions in document order and does not evaluate skip/terminate logic before rendering each page. TERM1 was physically the second question in the Screener block, immediately after S1. Every persona hit it as the next page and was terminated — no skip condition was ever evaluated. The same mechanism would have fired even if the survey had been published from the start; draft status was a red herring.

**What changed:** Removed the skip rule from S1 and deleted TERM1 entirely. "I am not a Columbia or Barnard student" is now an ordinary option that continues to Q2. The walk confirms S1 → Q2 → … → END with no other exits.

**Changes are saved as draft v2 — the survey is currently still serving live v1.** Reply **confirm** to push v2.

---

**Answer to 4:** The synthetic panel runner walks pages in document order. It does not evaluate skip logic, display conditions, or terminate blocks before advancing to the next page. Those are runner-side features that only fire in a real browser session. For synthetic panels, any terminate question placed in the question sequence will be hit as a regular page and will end the response — regardless of whether the skip that was supposed to route to it would have fired.
